data.name: REQUIRED SYNERGY WORKSHOP: Deja Damnation
data.detailed_description:
Try the Free Demo

Free Demo Available

The free demo contains the opening three chapters.
This is a slow-burn psychological horror game about surveillance, compliance, and a corporate training system that remembers how you behave.

Wishlist the full game to continue beyond the demo.


About the Game

You have been here before.

The room is familiar. The people are too. Small details refuse to line up, and every answer seems to outlive the moment that produced it.

Required Synergy Workshop: Deja Damnation is a psychological horror narrative adventure about identity, responsibility, and the pressure to become whatever other people need you to be.

The story unfolds across nine chapters and more than 25 major narrative sequences. Choices alter relationships, change later scenes, and leave consequences that may not become clear until much later.

Every Choice Leaves a Trace

Dialogue changes according to how you respond, who you trust, and what you choose to investigate. Characters remember your treatment of them, even when your own memory becomes difficult to trust.

Help can become leverage, trust can become obligation, and a choice that protects you may leave someone else carrying the damage.

Look Closer

Optional investigations reveal contradictions, missing context, and traces of events the main path only hints at.

Curiosity opens additional scenes and changes how later events are understood. The more you learn, the harder it becomes to accept anyone's version of events without asking what they gain from it.

The Story Continues Between Chapters

New conversations, messages, and investigations appear as the story progresses. Familiar spaces change over time, and relationships continue developing away from the main path.

People ask for help, loyalty, and silence. Small concessions can become expectations that are much harder to refuse.

  • Messages continue conversations outside major scenes and offer limited reply choices.

  • Dossiers collect conflicting information about characters, locations, and events.

  • Memory fragments preserve recovered images, sounds, and moments.

Visual Style

Deja Damnation combines 1990s-inspired anime with semi-real graphic-novel illustration, expressive linework, heavy screentone, analog texture, and a cold industrial palette.

Dialogue boxes, menus, camera views, and other interface elements become less reliable as the story progresses. Visual corruption develops alongside the narrative and changes how familiar scenes are read.

Full Game Scope

  • Nine main chapters

  • More than 25 major narrative sequences

  • Five evolving interchapter sections

  • Optional investigations

  • Persistent character relationships

  • Messages, dossiers, and memory fragments

  • Three endings

data.short_description: A slow-burn psychological horror narrative adventure where every choice leaves a trace. Across nine chapters, unstable memories and fragile relationships pull you into a story where trust always comes with a cost.
data.supported_languages:
English*, Japanese
*languages with full audio support

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i3-4130 or AMD FX-6300
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Intel HD Graphics 4400 or equivalent
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Standard onboard audio is sufficient.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-7400 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 750 Ti, AMD Radeon R7 360, or Intel Iris Xe
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: 1080p display recommended, SSD recommended for faster load times

- Flashing lights, glitches, screen shake
- Intense emotions, body horror, blood
